correctness.rationale: All pairs are faces, and the leaf simplex L is contractible. For root i, its leaf link has exactly two components: its own leaf is isolated and the other leaves contain the connected graph G−i in their link one-skeleton. After contracting L, the subcomplex containing at most one root per face is a wedge of the suspensions of these two-component links, each contributing one free generator by van Kampen. Collapse of L is valid for a contractible CW subcomplex. A nonadjacent root pair admits a leaf triangle at an internal vertex of a shortest root-to-root path; for adjacent roots a leaf triangle requires, and is equivalent to, equality of the third root's distances to the endpoints. Without such equality an adjacent pair occurs in no root triangle either, since a distance difference of one forces a geodesic equality. Pair every eligible new root edge with one permitted leaf triangle; each is a relative elementary expansion, while each unbalanced edge contributes a free circle. In the quotient by L, every non-own-leaf arrow from root i represents the same path class p_i, by coning a path in the connected link component. Thus every paired root edge represents p_i p_j^(−1), all unused root-leaf triangle relations are redundant, and every allowed three-root triangle telescopes to the identity. Higher cells do not affect π1. Abelianization gives integral H1 without torsion; bipartite distance parity and the odd-cycle antipodal witness give the corollaries (including v=3). The recorded homology computations, read along with their distance and elimination code, probe only finite graphs over finite fields; they neither establish freeness nor rule out integral torsion. No required computation substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The distinct result is the free-group rank formula for all bases with connected vertex deletions, using unbalanced edges to handle both bipartite and nonbipartite cases. The complete-bipartite restriction is already covered more strongly and is not credited as new. The wider bipartite and sunlet statements are evaluated as corollaries of the general classification, not as claims that every instance was previously unknown.
residual_risks: An unindexed or uninspected equivalent classification may exist, including in inaccessible sources. The full general classification is distinguished from actual accessible statements; no global priority assertion.

value.rationale: The classification computes a nonabelian invariant and explains which geometric features generate free circles, reducing an arbitrary simplicial presentation with many triangle relations to a distance test on edges. For example, a 5-cycle with one chord has both balanced and unbalanced edges, a case beyond the bipartite formula and cycle parity. The general rank law and redundant-triangle argument add substantive structure beyond enumeration or the earlier complete-bipartite subcase.
